label: Encomienda meaning
quiz: What is the key relationship introduced by encomienda in this lesson?
Tribute-collection rights with stated obligations
Automatic ownership of every field and resident
A voluntary gift from all households
A modern land deed covering all islands
retry: Why should a land claim be checked separately from a tribute grant?
Collection rights alone do not establish ownership of every field
Every payment record transfers all land
No land dispossession could ever happen
A collector's title proves every local right
hard: A caption says a grant automatically made all land private property. What correction fits?
Distinguish collection rights and seek separate land evidence
Keep the claim because all colonial arrangements are identical
Treat every resident as the holder's property
Replace evidence with an invented deed

label: Required payments
quiz: What distinguishes tribute from a freely offered present?
It is required under an authority
Its name proves every person freely chose it
It always had one identical amount
It reveals every household's resources
retry: What should a learner check before applying a recorded payment elsewhere?
The place, period, rules and circumstances
Only whether the number looks simple
A guessed modern price
An assumption that all years had identical rates
hard: A record lists goods paid in one setting. Which additional claim needs evidence?
That all households in every period owed identical goods and amounts
That goods appear in the record
That a payment can be investigated
That the document has a particular setting

label: Obligations and practice
quiz: A grant names a duty. What does that establish most directly?
A stated expectation, not proof of fulfillment
Proof every person was treated fairly
Proof every official obeyed perfectly
Every household's approval
retry: How should a learner use a debate about collection and obligations?
As evidence of disputed claims in context, not every community's complete story
As proof everyone agreed
As proof that one voice represents all people
As a substitute for examining actions
hard: A record promises protection but gives no account of action. What is needed?
Evidence of performance and effects on the people concerned
Only the promise repeated in larger letters
An invented statement of universal approval
A claim that promises always fulfill themselves

label: Household effects
quiz: Which question distinguishes demand from collection?
What was required and what was actually received?
Why were all amounts always identical?
Why is a fictional amount an authentic rule?
Which label guarantees fairness?
retry: What can a fictional household example establish?
An illustrated relationship, not an authentic universal tax rate
Every family's exact historical burden
One payment schedule for all colonial years
Every person's thoughts
hard: A receipt records goods received but gives no household information. What remains to investigate?
Resources and circumstances needed to assess the household effect
Only a larger title on the receipt
A claim that revenue equals everyone's wellbeing
An assumption that all demands were voluntary

label: Comparing records
quiz: Which record most directly raises a disputed practice or asks for a remedy?
A complaint
Only the title of an officeholder
An unlabelled teaching arrow
A definition without any recorded action
retry: A complaint has no reply in the available evidence. What is careful?
State the complaint and identify the unresolved outcome
Assume relief was granted
Assume every resident approved
Invent a decision to fill the gap
hard: Why compare a grant, collection account and complaint?
They can address different parts of rights, practice and disputed effects
Each must contain every person's view
A grant alone proves all outcomes
A missing reply proves no local person acted
